analysis.title: GS DeGrasse - Macro & Cyclicals remain in focus .. EPS Feedback .. 14 Oct 2026
key_insights: Day 2 of bank earnings: the tape is choppy and driven by shifting macro and datacenter concerns. When AI trades higher, Financials have often traded lower (inverse correlation). When the market worries about the AI capex buildout and its funding, the link between Financials, capital markets and AI is re-established.
Rates round-tripped the morning's CPI print. Financials are off the lows, but the tape is moving against stocks levered to economic growth, with a clear tilt toward defensive exposure.

GS's Long cyclicals vs Defensives basket is down 6% from early October levels. The desk asks whether the rest of the market's cyclical exposure is catching up to what Financials and capital markets have signaled for a month.

Sentiment on earnings reactions is sharply negative, and investors are weighting negative datapoints more heavily than positive ones. The desk calls some of it narrative piling on to price action and could not find a reason for Citigroup's underperformance the day before.

The desk says price action is questioning the level of earnings growth, not credit issues (see bank P/TBV multiples). Credit quality is near the bottom of the list of debates. Investors are focused on pipelines and capital markets backlogs, capital, operating leverage and margin levers.

BAC is down 5% as of send (indicated -8% pre-market). Feedback: the quarter matched what the bank guided to mid-quarter (weaker trading, no expense offset) but was worse than indicated. The 2027 NII guide was better, yet the stock failed to rally, which prompted questions from longer-duration investors.

BAC bulls emphasize that the NII-upside story is intact. Bears point to CET1 capital at 10.9% with GSIB surcharge pressure at the start of the new year, so there is little excess capital. The buyback may have to slow or balance sheet growth may be pulled back. Bears also argue that regulatory focus may limit expense levers if revenue slows.

PGR is down 6% on slower growth and weaker margin in Personal Auto. Insurance specialists cite a slowdown in Direct and worsening pricing (agency/direct annualized premium per policy -5.0%/-3.6%). Pushback calls the move an overreaction to a worse-than-expected monthly print.

STT is down 6%. Asset Servicing and other fees missed on the top line, while NII and NIM were slightly better. The implied 4Q guide is about 5% below GS estimates, while the buyside expected upside. Bears were emboldened given the stock's +35% YTD move and premium multiple versus its 5-year history. Flows in the trust bank space have picked up.

MS is down 3%. Wealth pre-tax margin missed consensus by 30bps. The broader overhang is macro, rates, the cycle and datacenter noise. The 3Q normalization in IB and Trading was better than feared. The market is discounting the pace of forward earnings growth.

BLK is flat after a strong quarter with next to zero pushback (desk crowding score was 8/10). Organic fee growth was 11% against a bogey of 8-9%. Adjusted margin was 47.8% versus 45.9% last quarter and 44.5% the quarter before. Bulls say the stock is underappreciated and has a deep moat and a business model they see as immune to disruption.

earnings_insights: BAC Q3 reported: the quarter matched the mid-quarter guide of weaker trading and no expense offset, but was worse than indicated. The 2027 NII guide was better. CET1 capital is 10.9% (reported), with GSIB pressure at the start of the new year. Stock down 5% as of send.
PGR reported: Personal Auto growth slowed and margin weakened. Agency/direct annualized premium per policy was -5.0%/-3.6% (reported). Stock down 6%.
STT reported: Asset Servicing and other fees missed on the top line, while NII and NIM were slightly better. The implied 4Q guide is about 5% below GS estimate. Stock down 6%.
MS reported: Wealth pre-tax margin missed consensus by 30bps. IB and Trading normalization in 3Q was better than feared. Stock down 3%.

BLK reported: organic fee growth was 11% (reported) versus a bogey of 8-9%. Adjusted margin was 47.8% (reported), versus 45.9% last quarter and 44.5% the quarter before. Blostein estimates a margin of about 49% adjusted for performance fees. Stock flat.
